title: CHROME: Concurrency-Aware Holistic Cache Management Framework with Online Reinforcement Learning
problem: Existing cache management approaches focus on individual techniques (replacement, bypassing, prefetching) and rely on static, intuition-driven policies that perform poorly under complex and dynamic multi-core workloads with no joint optimization across techniques.
motivation: Coordinated optimization of cache management techniques can significantly improve system performance in multi-core environments where cache contention and concurrency effects substantially impact throughput.
method: CHROME uses reinforcement learning (a technique where the system learns by trying approaches and getting feedback on results) to make cache decisions in real-time based on what the program is currently doing. It combines three techniques: removing old data to make space (cache replacement), skipping the cache entirely for some data (cache bypassing), and predicting and loading data that will likely be needed soon (prefetching). For each decision, the system receives a score based on whether it was correct and whether it improved overall system performance, allowing it to continuously improve.
key_novelty: CHROME jointly optimizes cache replacement, bypassing, and prefetching through real-time learning that adapts to concurrent workloads, rather than optimizing each technique separately with fixed rules.
contributions: Holistic framework integrating cache replacement, bypassing, and pattern-based prefetching
Online reinforcement learning for dynamic, workload-adaptive cache policy optimization
Concurrency-aware design addressing multi-core system effects
13.7% performance improvement over LRU in multi-core systems with modest overhead
primary_theme: dynamic cache management with reinforcement learning
